name: European Russia (Moscow · St Petersburg · west of the Urals)

language.script_notes: White-with-black-base sign poles and big blue direction signs apply here too.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Concrete/metal posts in regional colour schemes (red-and-white or black-and-white).
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; better maintained near Moscow and St Petersburg, rougher further out.
road_furniture.line_paint: White centre and edge lines on the M-roads and main routes; minor roads often unmarked.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: White sign poles with a black band at the base. Concrete 'holey' utility poles. The road network is densest and best-surfaced here of anywhere in Russia.

architecture.roof_style: Flat Soviet block roofs; pitched roofs and onion domes on older buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Dense Soviet panel blocks in the cities; imperial-era stone and stucco in the historic centres (St Petersburg especially); log izby with carved nalichniki in the villages of the Golden Ring.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey concrete, ochre and pale green stucco; blue, green and white wooden houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: St Petersburg's imperial architecture; the Kremlin-and-cathedral old towns of the Golden Ring; endless panel-block suburbs; wooden village houses with painted window frames.

nature.vegetation: Mixed and broadleaf forest in the west and centre — birch, oak, linden — grading into darker spruce-pine taiga toward the north; heavily farmed black-earth on the southern fringe.
nature.terrain: The flat East European Plain, barely rippled by the low Valdai and Central Russian uplands, drained by big slow rivers (Volga, Oka, Don headwaters).
nature.climate_signature: Cold continental with reliably snowy winters, but milder than Siberia; overcast grey skies are common, and much coverage is late-autumn or winter.

vehicles.plate_color: White with a region number — low numbers and the Moscow/St Petersburg codes (77/97/99/78/98 and their 1xx, 7xx variants) dominate here.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Ladas plus a large share of modern foreign cars; left-hand drive throughout (unlike the Far East).

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 and Gen 4; the black-car-with-antenna appears here.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: The densest, most complete coverage in Russia, including full city networks.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic, panel blocks, birch woodland, wooden houses — almost indistinguishable at a glance
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Belarus is visibly tidier and smoother-surfaced, uses plates without a region-number box, and occasionally shows Belarusian spelling.
European Russia has more broadleaf forest, better roads, denser towns and imperial-era architecture; Siberia is emptier, more wooden, more larch, snowier and rougher.
Ukrainian plates carry a blue EU-style strip; Ukrainian orthography uses і, ї, є.
